<STRUCT_0001>
An algebraic stack is a stack in groupoids over the category of schemes
with the fppf topology that has a diagonal representable by algebraic
spaces and is the target of a surjective smooth morphism from a scheme.
See Algebraic Stacks, Section <REF_0001>.
A ``Deligne-Mumford stack'' is an algebraic stack for which there exists
a scheme and a surjective <ACCENT_0001>tale morphism from that scheme to it
as in the paper <REF_0002> of Deligne and Mumford, see
Algebraic Stacks, Definition <REF_0003>.
We will reserve the term ``Artin stack'' for a stack such as in the papers by
Artin, see <REF_0004>, <REF_0005>, and <REF_0006>.
A possible definition is that an Artin stack is an algebraic stack
<MATH_0001> over a locally Noetherian scheme <MATH_0002> such that
<MATH_0003> is
locally of finite type<FOOTNOTEOPEN_0001>Namely, these are exactly the algebraic
stacks over <MATH_0004> satisfying Artin's axioms [-1], [0], [1], [2], [3], [4], [5]
of Artin's Axioms, Section <REF_0007>.<FOOTNOTECLOSE_0001>.
